assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks unite a beautiful control of atomic quantum systems with a profound advance in precision measurement.
assessment.attribution: Katori originated the lattice-clock concept and Ye made decisive experimental advances; the pairing is clear and balanced.
assessment.maturity: Independent laboratories have achieved extraordinary performance and the clocks now underpin a mature field.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Their proposals established a powerful physical route to quantum computation and simulation with trapped atomic systems.
assessment.attribution: Cirac and Zoller made the foundational joint theoretical contribution represented by this nomination.
assessment.maturity: The ideas have guided decades of precise experiments and now form a broad, thriving experimental platform.
uncertainties: The boundary between foundational proposals and later trapped-ion implementations needs careful prize definition.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Strongly interacting Fermi gases made a clean, tunable many-body system in which universal quantum behavior can be tested quantitatively.
assessment.attribution: Several groups made essential independent contributions; these proposed experimental leaders are defensible but the three-person limit is restrictive.
assessment.maturity: The phenomena have been repeatedly observed, precisely characterized, and connected to a wide body of many-body theory.
uncertainties: Rudolf Grimm is also a major contributor and attribution cannot be fully represented by three names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum error correction supplied the physical and conceptual answer to protecting quantum information from unavoidable noise.
assessment.attribution: Shor, Steane, and Kitaev made distinct foundational contributions to the central codes and fault-tolerance framework.
assessment.maturity: The principle is firmly established and increasingly tested in hardware, although fully fault-tolerant computation remains incomplete.
uncertainties: The ultimate scale and practical threshold performance of quantum error correction are still being established.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum control of mechanical motion extends quantum measurement and state preparation into systems visible on a human-made scale.
assessment.attribution: The proposed names represent complementary experimental breakthroughs in an international development with substantial wider contributions.
assessment.maturity: Ground-state cooling, quantum-limited measurement, and coherent control have been reproduced across several platforms.
uncertainties: Whether the body of work has yet yielded a single sufficiently distinct discovery for a prize needs scrutiny.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Photonic crystals revealed how periodic structure can control the electromagnetic density of states and light propagation in a fundamentally new way.
assessment.attribution: Yablonovitch, John, and Joannopoulos supplied central experimental and theoretical foundations.
assessment.maturity: The field is long-established, experimentally robust, and has generated many physical realizations and applications.
uncertainties: The relative weight of foundational discovery versus subsequent engineering applications requires careful framing.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Geometric quantum phases have changed our understanding of phase, interference, and topology, with deep consequences across physics.
assessment.attribution: Aharonov and Berry introduced distinct seminal phase concepts; the nomination combines related but historically separate contributions.
assessment.maturity: Both effects have extensive experimental confirmation and have become standard physical tools.
uncertainties: A single prize formulation joining the Aharonov-Bohm and Berry phases may obscure their distinct origins and attribution.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: High-energy astrophysical neutrinos opened a genuinely new observational window on the violent universe.
assessment.attribution: Halzen was a central scientific leader, but the discovery was necessarily achieved by a large IceCube collaboration.
assessment.maturity: The signal has persisted and neutrino astronomy has developed beyond the original observation.
uncertainties: The appropriate individual attribution within a very large collaboration remains difficult.
